name: Falciparum malaria, carried by Anopheles mosquitoes
_doc: As trypanosomiasis.json. Host 'people': annual_loss_at_full_challenge is an excess death rate per year for each demography band (children, working_age, elderly), added to baseline mortality and scaled by the disease burden the nation has not yet removed.

challenge_envelope.source: Mordecai et al. 2013 Ecology Letters 16:22, abstract via USGS (pubs.usgs.gov/publication/70125667): 'predicts optimal malaria transmission at 25 C' and 'transmission decreases dramatically at temperatures > 28 C'; the 17 to 34 C limits are quoted from Ryan et al., Mapping physiological suitability limits for malaria in Africa under climate change (arXiv 1407.7612): 'temperatures between 17-34 C (Mordecai et al. 2013)'. The lower edge of the optimum (22 C) has no source found. Rainfall edges: no source found (Craig et al. 1999 not opened)

hosts.people.source: Malaria deaths before control fell mostly on children under five in holoendemic areas, of order one to two percent of them a year, a few per thousand of adults who have acquired partial immunity (Snow et al. 2005 Nature 434:214; Hay et al. 2004). No pre-industrial death register exists, so the rates are an order of magnitude only.
